skeleton:
Garlic-Thyme Field Mushrooms

British · Easy · Serves 2

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The weekend version of the breakfast mushroom: large flat field or portobello caps cooked cut-face down in butter that has been visited by garlic and thyme, basted until their gills flood with juices and the whole pan smells like a farmhouse kitchen. Where the buttered button mushrooms are the weekday quick-fry, the field mushroom is a knife-and-fork component — a cap that holds a pool of garlicky butter and delivers it to the plate in one spoonable piece. The technique is basting a big cap, not frying a small one: the butter goes in aromatised (garlic and thyme steeped in it off-heat, so the garlic turns golden and sweet rather than bitter), the cap cooks cut-face down in it, and the spoon delivers it over the top repeatedly. The cap's own juices join the butter in the pan — that liquor is the dish.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The mushrooms

The aromatics

  • they steep without burning)

To finish

- **Wipe, never wash** — the standing rule. A damp cloth takes off the soil; a rinse starts the water clock that ends the crust. - **Slice the garlic** — thin slices steep in the butter and turn sweet-golden over the cook's ten minutes; crushed garlic hits the hot butter and burns bitter in ninety seconds. The slice is the safety. - Trim the stems flush so the caps sit flat, cut-face down, in the pan.

Garlic-Thyme Field Mushrooms

Prep: 5 minutes · Cook: 10 minutes · Total: 15 minutes · Serves 2

Ingredients

The mushrooms

  • 4 large flat field mushrooms or 2 portobello caps (about 400 g), stems trimmed flush, wiped clean
  • 30 g unsalted butter
  • 10 ml / 10 g olive oil

The aromatics

  • 2 garlic cloves, thinly sliced (slices, not crushed — they steep without burning)
  • 4 sprigs fresh thyme (or 1 g dried)
  • 2 g fine sea salt
  • 1 g black pepper

To finish

  • 5 g parsley or chives, chopped (optional)
  • A squeeze of lemon (5 ml), optional

Instructions

  1. **Aromatise the butter, off to a golden start.** Melt the butter with the oil in a wide pan over medium heat, add the garlic slices and thyme sprigs, and cook 60–90 seconds until the garlic's edges turn pale gold — fragrant, not browned. Checkpoint — the butter foams gently, smells of thyme and sweet garlic, and the slices are golden at their thinnest edges with their centres still pale. Burnt-garlic smell means the heat was high — restart the butter; it is a two-minute ingredient.
  2. **The caps, cut-face down, 5 minutes.** Lay the caps cut-face down in the aromatised butter and season their tops. Cook undisturbed 4–5 minutes — the cut faces brown while the caps' juices begin to weep into the pan and mingle with the butter. Checkpoint — the cut faces are chestnut-brown in patches, the caps have flattened and softened, and the pan holds a darkening, foaming liquor of butter and mushroom juice. A cap lifted shows a browned, not pale, face.
  3. **Turn and baste, 4 minutes.** Turn the caps gill-side down and cook 4 minutes more, spooning the garlic-thyme butter over their tops continuously — every 20 seconds, a spoonful. The liquor reduces and concentrates around them. Checkpoint — the caps are collapsed and glossy, their liquor reduced to a few dark, syrupy spoonfuls in the pan, and a knife tip into the thickest part of a cap meets no resistance. The gills hold a pool of the butter-juice — the dish's sauce, sitting where the plate wants it.
  4. **Finish and land.** Off the heat, scatter the herbs, add the lemon if using, and tilt each cap onto the plate gill-cup up, spooning the pan's liquor into the cup and over the top. Checkpoint — each cap arrives as a small, glossy vessel of garlicky butter-juice, browned outside, tender within — and the first forkful cuts through like a steak, releasing the liquor into the yolk or the toast beside it. This is the breakfast mushroom promoted to a plate's headliner.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Garlic burnt and bitterCrushed garlic, or heat too highSliced garlic, medium heat, golden-not-brown
Caps watery and paleWashed mushrooms or a cool panWipe only; the butter foams before the caps land
No liquor in the panHeat too high, evaporated too fast, or mushrooms old and dryMedium heat; add a spoonful of water if the pan dries before the caps are tender
Caps raw at the thick rimUnder-cookedThe knife-tip test; 2 more minutes basting

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **Cooked caps keep 3 days refrigerated** and reheat in a covered pan with a spoon of water — they improve, as mushrooms do overnight. The aromatised butter can be made ahead and holds a week. - **Variation — the filled field mushroom:** after basting, fill the cup with 30 g of grated Cheddar or the black pudding crumb and flash under the grill — the cap becomes a dish. - **Variation — the toast topper:** one cap, butter-liquor and all, on thick buttered toast with a poached egg — the smallest complete breakfast on the site. - **On the plate:** this is the button mushroom's weekend sibling and the portobello master's pan-cooked cousin — same vegetable, three registers, all of them worth the butter.
